intended_object: The function that sends an R-valued unitriangular matrix in the r-th superdiagonal stage subgroup to the evaluation K-algebra map from the stage's quotient coordinate ring to R. It is the forward half of the bijection between points of the stage and the subgroup. Inferred from the docstring and from its use as `toFun` of `unitriangularStageMulEquivAlgHom`.
explanation:
The body takes the existing evaluation map `unitriangularFromGL`, which sends a unitriangular matrix to a K-algebra map out of the ambient coordinate ring. It then passes this map through `Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ` to the quotient by the stage ideal. The proof that the ideal lies in the kernel uses `mem_stage_iff` together with the membership of `s` in the stage subgroup. So the definition correctly builds the evaluation of a point of the stage.

It has no standalone mathematical role, though. It is the `toFun` piece used to build the group isomorphism `unitriangularStageMulEquivAlgHom`, which says that the stage Hopf quotient represents the subgroup. It only serves to set up that representability isomorphism (the companion theorems `_comp_quotient`, `_toGL_fromGL` and `_fromGL_toGL` support it). It is not a mathematical notion that would be judged on its own, so it counts as an auxiliary construction rather than a definition of a mathematical object.
